question: A 61-year-old woman presents to her primary care provider with complaints of fatigue, weight gain of 5.5 kg (12.1 lb) and intermittent nausea over the past 4 months. She denies any changes to her diet. She has had type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 27 years complicated by diabetic neuropathy. Vital signs include: temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F), blood pressure 167/98 mm Hg and pulse 80/min. Physical examination reveals bilateral pitting lower-extremity edema. Fundoscopic examination reveals bilateral micro-aneurysms and cotton wool patches. Her serum creatinine is 2.6 mg/dL. Which of the following is the best initial therapy for this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Type 2 diabetes mellitus for 27 years" -> "Diabetic neuropathy" -> "Weight gain and fatigue" -> "Possible diabetic nephropathy" -> 70% CHAIN: "Type 2 diabetes mellitus for 27 years" -> "Diabetic neuropathy" -> "Weight gain and fatigue" -> "Hypertension (167/98 mm Hg)" -> "Renal impairment (serum creatinine 2.6 mg/dL)" -> 80% CHAIN: "Type 2 diabetes mellitus for 27 years" -> "Diabetic neuropathy" -> "Weight gain and fatigue" -> "Hypertension (167/98 mm Hg)" -> "Renal impairment (serum creatinine 2.6 mg/dL)" -> "Bilateral pitting lower-extremity edema" -> "Nephrotic syndrome" -> 75% CHAIN: "Type 2 diabetes mellitus for 27 years" -> "Diabetic neuropathy" -> "Weight gain and fatigue" -> "Hypertension (167/98 mm Hg)" -> "Renal impairment (serum creatinine 2.6 mg/dL)" -> "Bilateral pitting lower-extremity edema" -> "Nephrotic syndrome" -> "Best initial therapy: ACE inhibitor like Perindopril" -> 70%
enhanced_information: The patient with long-standing type 2 diabetes mellitus, diabetic neuropathy, weight gain, fatigue, hypertension, renal impairment, and bilateral pitting lower-extremity edema likely has diabetic nephropathy. The best initial therapy for this patient is an ACE inhibitor like Perindopril, which can help manage both hypertension and renal complications in diabetic nephropathy.
analysis: The patient's presentation with long-standing type 2 diabetes mellitus, diabetic neuropathy, weight gain, fatigue, hypertension, renal impairment, and bilateral pitting lower-extremity edema is suggestive of diabetic nephropathy. Given the presence of hypertension and renal complications, the best initial therapy for this patient is an ACE inhibitor like Perindopril, which can help manage both conditions effectively.
